stem:
Fig. 6.1 shows a circuit that rectifies an alternating input voltage *V*ᵢₙ and produces an output voltage *V*ₒᵤₜ across a resistor *R*.

[[fig:f1]]

The four terminals of the rectification circuit are labelled W, X, Y and Z.
A capacitor *C* is connected in parallel with resistor *R*.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by rectification.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 6.2 shows the variations with time *t* of the potential differences (p.d.s) *V*ᵢₙ and *V*ₒᵤₜ.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
The variation of *V*ᵢₙ with *t* can be represented by

*V*ᵢₙ = *A* cos *Bt*

where *A* and *B* are constants.

Determine the values of *A* and *B*. Give a unit with your answer for *A*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the type of rectification produced by the circuit in Fig. 6.1.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 6.3, draw the circuit diagram for the components inside the rectification circuit.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Determine a value for the time constant for the discharge of the capacitor *C* through the resistor *R* in Fig. 6.1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The capacitor *C* has a capacitance of 570 μF.

Use your answer in (b)(iv) to determine the resistance of resistor *R*.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.1
figures.alt: A rectification circuit block with terminals W, X, Y and Z connected to an input voltage and an output circuit containing a capacitor in parallel with a resistor.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.2
figures.alt: A graph of input and output potential difference against time, showing a sinusoidal input and a rectified, smoothed output.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.3
figures.alt: A blank dashed rectangle for drawing a circuit, with terminals W and X on the left and Y and Z on the right.
